newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast to hold postponed poll December 29.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast to hold postponed poll December 29.

text.p: Ivory Coast will hold legislative and municipal elections in and around the western opposition stronghold of Gagnoa on December 29 to conclude 1995 national elections disrupted by political and ethnic violence.
A cabinet statement, published in the government newspaper Fraternite Matin on Saturday, included decrees setting the date of the polls.
The ruling Democratic Party won landslide victories in the West African nation's second multi-party legislative elections in November 1995 and municipal elections in February 1996.

But the government postponed polling around Gagnoa, hotbed of protest surrounding Democratic Party leader Henri Konan Bedie's October 1995 election as president in a poll boycotted by the main opposition.

Political and ethnic violence surrounding the poll killed 35 people nationwide, of whom 25 were killed in the Gagnoa region in ethnic attacks pitting indigenous Betes, who support the opposition, and migrant farmers from Bedie's Baoule tribe.

Laurent Gbagbo and his Ivorian Popular Front spearheaded the opposition's 1990 campaign that forced independence president Felix Houphouet-Boigny to agree to multi-party politics. Bedie succeeded Houphouet on his death in 1993.
Three of the parliament's 175 seats are at stake in or round Gagnoa. The ruling party holds 148 seats, the opposition 21.

Three others will be contested on December 29 -- in Adzope in the east and Seguela in the north, where the 1995 results were annulled, and in Korhogo in the north where an opposition Rally of the Republicans legislator died.
